pool.prompt: Which occupation kept written tax records?
options: Scribe
Farmer
Potter
pool.rationale: Correct: Scribe. See Assigned OER Ancient Egypt, pages 15, 16, 17.

repair.prompt: Who would most likely write down the number of soldiers in an army?
options: A scribe
A herder
A potter
repair.teach: An occupation is a job. A contribution is what that work provides for society. Name the job, describe what the person does, and connect the work to what others need. Scribes read, wrote and kept records, including taxes, court cases and a census, which is a population count. Artisans made goods such as pottery, furniture and jewelry. Farmers grew food and useful crops and raised animals. Food surplus means extra food beyond what is needed. A surplus helped some people specialize in other jobs. People depended on one another’s work.

People depended on one another’s work. For three specific contributions, name different useful tasks. Scribes could keep tax records, count soldiers and record a census. A tax record helps officials track what was collected; a census records the population; food and useful crops support people in other occupations. Three different words for one task are not three different contributions.

They answer every historical question by themselves.
They prove all Egyptians lived as royalty.

Those objects help researchers study royal burial, craftsmanship and beliefs about the afterlife. Tomb objects are evidence of this royal burial. They do not prove every Egyptian owned the same goods or received the same burial.

A pyramid is a monumental building used as a royal tomb in ancient Egypt. Its purpose connects architecture, royal power and afterlife beliefs. Not every Egyptian was buried in a pyramid. Giza and the Valley of the Kings are different burial places. Khufu’s Great Pyramid is at Giza; Tutankhamun’s tomb is in the Valley of the Kings. Do not use these place names as if they were one site.

repairPool.chapterTitle: Mummies, tombs and preserving the body
repairPool.teaching: A mummy is a preserved body. Mummification is the process used to preserve a body. Embalming means treating a body to slow decay. In the process described in the reading, embalmers cleaned the body, treated organs, used natron to dry it and wrapped it in linen. Canopic jars held certain organs. Details changed over Egypt’s long history. Keep object and process separate: mummy = the preserved body; mummification = preparing and preserving it. Afterlife beliefs explain why this work mattered.

repairPool.prompt: Which region was farther upstream: Upper or Lower Egypt?
options: Upper Egypt
Lower Egypt
Both were at the river’s mouth
repairPool.rationale: Correct: Upper Egypt. The Nile flows north into the Mediterranean Sea. Upper Egypt is in the south, upstream. Lower Egypt is in the north, downstream, near the Nile Delta. Upper and Lower describe positions along the river. They do not mean top and bottom on a page. Follow the river toward its mouth to move downstream. Remember the pair: Upper Egypt = south and upstream; Lower Egypt = north and downstream, near the delta.

repair.teach: Hieroglyphics is the classroom term for Egyptian writing using hieroglyphs. Signs could represent sounds or words; it was not simply an English letter-for-picture code. Papyrus is a Nile plant and the paper-like writing material made from its stems. Scribes used writing skills to record information. Writing is a system of signs; papyrus is a material. The Rosetta Stone contains three scripts: hieroglyphic, demotic and Greek, using two languages. The assigned text simplifies this incorrectly. Comparing the same message helped scholars decipher the writing.
